q: Infants who weigh less than how much must ride in a rear-facing child car seat?
a: 9 kg (20 lb)
e: Under 9 kg: rear-facing. 9–18 kg: car seat with tether. 18–36 kg (under 8, under 145 cm): booster.
s: Infants who weigh less than 9 kilograms (20 lbs.) must be buckled into a rear-facing child car seat

q: A child may stop using a booster seat and wear a seatbelt when they…
a: Turn 8, OR weigh 36 kg (80 lb), OR are 145 cm (4'9") tall
e: Any ONE of the three is enough, if they can wear the belt properly.
s: The child turns eight years old.

q: Your car has airbags. Do you still need to wear your seatbelt?
a: Yes: airbags don't replace seatbelts
e: In a collision, your seatbelt keeps you in position so the airbag can protect you.
s: Airbags do not replace seatbelts.

q: Where must you NEVER put a rear-facing child car seat?
a: In a seat with an active airbag
w: In the middle of the back seat
e: If the airbag inflates, it could seriously injure the child. The back seat is best.
s: Never put a rear-facing child car seat in a seating position that has an active airbag.

q: Which of these is NOT part of Ontario's distracted driving law, but could still get you charged with careless driving?
a: Eating or drinking while driving
w: Watching a video on a phone
e: Eating, drinking, grooming and reaching aren't in the distracted driving law, but careless driving charges can apply.
s: Other actions such as eating, drinking, grooming, smoking, reading and reaching for objects are not part of Ontario’s distracted driving law. However, you can still be charged with careless or dangerous driving.

q: You have more passengers than seatbelts. Can two small children share one belt?
a: No: never put more than one person in a seatbelt
e: Sharing a belt can cause serious injury or death in a collision.
s: Never put more than one person into a seatbelt; this can cause serious injury or even death in a collision.

q: You're driving and start yawning, drifting in your lane and can't remember the last few kilometres. What should you do?
a: Pull off the road somewhere safe and take a nap
w: Open the window and turn up the radio
Drive faster to get home sooner
e: Stimulants are never a substitute for sleep. You can fall asleep without knowing it.
s: Pull off the road and park your vehicle in a safe, secure place.

q: You think an angry driver is following you. What should you do?
a: Don't drive home: drive to a police station or a busy public place
w: Drive home and lock the door
Pull over and talk to them
e: If you feel threatened, stay in your car with the doors locked and call police.
s: If you believe you are being followed, do not drive home. Drive to a police station or a busy public place.

q: Another driver is threatening you. What should you do?
a: Stay in your car, lock the doors, call police, and use your horn and signals to get attention
w: Follow them to get their plate number
e: Don't return aggression. Avoid eye contact and don't gesture back.
s: Stay in your vehicle and lock the doors.

q: A deer is standing on the road ahead. What should you do?
a: Slow down and sound your horn; don't try to drive around it
w: Flash your high beams and keep your speed
e: Animals move unpredictably. Watch for others nearby, too.
s: Slow down and sound your horn.

q: Driving at night, you see shining eyes at the side of the road. What should you do?
a: Slow down and be ready to stop
e: It's probably an animal that may bolt onto the road.
s: If you do see shining eyes, slow down and be ready to stop.

q: You're driving through a construction zone. What should you do?
a: Drive carefully, don't change lanes, and be ready for sudden stops
w: Change lanes often to find the fastest one
e: Watch for workers and construction vehicles, too.
s: do not change lanes, be ready for sudden stops and watch for workers and related construction vehicles and equipment on the road

q: You've just had an argument and you're very angry. What should you do?
a: Don't drive until you've calmed down
w: Drive fast to blow off steam
e: Strong emotions reduce your ability to think and react quickly.
s: Don't drive when you are upset or angry. Strong emotions can reduce your ability to think and react quickly.

q: Mirrors can't show everything. What is the only way to make sure your blind spot is clear?
a: Turn your head and do a shoulder check
e: Blind spots are usually behind you on the left and right.
s: turning your head to do shoulder checks is the only way to make sure there is nothing in your blind spots

q: Who is responsible for making sure passengers under 16 are buckled up?
a: The driver
w: The passengers' parents, wherever they sit
e: Drivers can be fined and get demerit points if a passenger under 16 isn't properly buckled.
s: As a driver, you are responsible for ensuring that all passengers under 16 years of age are properly buckled into a seatbelt, child car seat or booster seat.

q: What is the penalty for a driver who doesn't wear a seatbelt?
a: A fine and 2 demerit points
e: Buckle up every time.
s: Drivers who do not buckle up can be fined and will be given two demerit points.

q: A G1 or G2 driver doesn't have a working seatbelt for every passenger. What can happen?
a: They can lose their licence for at least 30 days
w: Nothing, if the trip is short
e: Novice drivers must have a working seatbelt for every passenger.
s: Drivers who do not ensure there is a working seatbelt for every passenger can lose their licence for at least 30 days.

q: What kind of seatbelt must you use with a booster seat?
a: A lap AND shoulder belt
w: No seatbelt; the booster holds the child
e: Never use a lap belt alone with a booster seat.
s: You must use a booster seat with a lap/shoulder belt.

q: You hit a deer or a moose. Who should you report it to?
a: The local police or the Ministry of Natural Resources
e: Don't try to move an injured animal.
s: If you hit a deer or moose, report it to the local police service or the Ministry of Natural Resources.

q: Which rule about your car windows is correct?
a: They must not be coated with anything that stops you from seeing out in any direction
w: Only the back window must be clear
e: Also, the windshield and front side windows must not be coated so people can't see in.
s: The windows of your vehicle must not be coated with any material that keeps you from seeing out in any direction.
